podcast.title: Suspected Green Day Identity
podcast.body: The Network, despite denials from Billie Joe Armstrong, is widely suspected to be a pseudonymous project of Green Day. Evidence includes Armstrong's ownership of their label, Adeline Records, biographical lyrical references on their album Money Money 2020, visual similarities (such as "The Snew's nose" to Tré Cool's), the band's website being registered to Green Day Inc., and their single live performance opening for Green Day on October 13, 2005. "No idea who these people are, but it's widely suspected that all three members of Green Day are somehow involved."

xref.title: SNL Fallout and CD Steamrolling (1992)
xref.body: The Pope photo incident led to immediate and intense backlash: she was egged outside Rockefeller Center, NBC received nearly 5,000 complaint calls, and she was banned from the network. A pile of her CDs and tapes were publicly steamrolled outside her New York record company's offices, an event she and a friend found amusing enough to attend in disguise and even be interviewed by a local reporter. "A pile of her CDs and tapes were literally steamrolled in front of the offices of her New York record company."

xref.title: "The Puppy Episode" (1997) – Coming Out Storyline
xref.body: This two-part episode saw DeGeneres' character, Ellen Morgan, a cheerful, neurotic bookstore manager, realize she was a lesbian. The episode was co-written by Ellen herself and originally aired on ABC on April 30, 1997. The title "The Puppy episode" was used as a code name to keep the coming-out storyline a secret, and also referenced an executive's reported suggestion that Ellen Morgan "get a puppy instead" when the network was initially approached with the idea. "When word got out about the impending coming out episode, hate mail poured into Ellen's offices."

xref.title: Atlantic Records Signing
xref.body: The band's substantial fanbase, cultivated through performances in Christian-friendly clubs across the U.S., ultimately led to their discovery and signing by Atlantic Records. P.O.D. became one of the pioneering bands to successfully cross over from the "Christian Underground" into the mainstream "Heathen Rock" world. "Eventually and thanks to the network of fans POD had amassed in the Christian friendly clubs across the US they were discovered and signed by Atlantic Records."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Billy Joe Armstrong's Alias
xref.body: Billie Joe Armstrong, Green Day's frontman, is known to have written songs under the alias "Will Him Think." This fact, along with his ownership of Adeline Records (which released The Network's album), contributes to the widespread suspicion that Green Day is behind The Network, despite Armstrong's denials. "It is a fact that Billy Joe has written songs under the alias Will Him Think."

xref.title: Confirmed Green Day Side Project
xref.body: Foxboro Hot Tubs is a "Garage Band side project" that Green Day undertook with friends to "blow up some creative steam" following their work on the American Idiot album. Unlike other pseudonymous projects, Green Day has been completely transparent about this identity, with Billie Joe Armstrong explicitly stating, "The only similarity between Foxboro Hot Tops and Green Day is that we are the same band." They even performed live unmasked, sometimes covering songs by The Network, their other suspected alter ego. "The only similarity between Foxboro Hot Tops and Green Day is that we are the same band, said Billy Joe Armstrong."

xref.title: Show's Origin as a Late-Night Special
xref.body: In 1989, NBC approached Jerry Seinfeld and Larry David not for a sitcom, but to write and produce a 90-minute late-night special. Instead, they wrote a 30-minute script for a pilot, "The Seinfeld Chronicles." "When NBC approached Jerry Seinfeld and Larry David in 1989, the network wasn't actually looking for a sitcom. They asked the writing duo to write and produce a 90-minute late-night special."

xref.title: The Network Identity Speculation
xref.body: The band The Network released *Money Money 2020* in 2003 through Adeline Records, a label owned by Billy Joe Armstrong. Given The Network's sound resemblance to Green Day, it was speculated that this was actually Green Day performing material from the allegedly stolen *Cigarettes and Valentines* sessions, a claim Billy Joe Armstrong denied. "In 2003, a weird band called The Network released a record called Money, Money, 2020 through Adeline Records, which oddly enough is a label owned by Billy Joe Armstrong. Now The Network sounded an awful lot like Green Day. Was this actually Green Day performing cigarettes and Valentine's? Billy Joe says, oh no! But I don't trust him."
